name: Intoxication and substance-related offenses
description: Legal constructs addressing public drunkenness, driving under the influence, and controlled-substance rules—an imperfect but recurring legal analogue to moral warnings about intemperance and disordered appetite (including gluttony in its broader classical sense).
foundationStrengthRationale: Policy shifts between prohibition, harm reduction, and medical models complicate any simple moral mapping.

pros.claim: Targets acute public-safety risks from impaired judgment and coordination.
pros.evidence: DUI/DWI regimes and public-intoxication laws are widespread responses to measurable harms.

cons.claim: Gluttony as a spiritual vice is a poor fit for addiction science and socioeconomic drivers of substance use.
cons.evidence: Public-health literature distinguishes disease, dependence, and moral fault in ways classical vice lists did not.
